data.name: Mauritius
data.summary: Mauritius has no capital gains tax, no inheritance, estate or gift tax and no wealth tax. Residents are taxed at 0/10/20% on income, but foreign-source income is taxed only when remitted to Mauritius, and dividends from Mauritian companies are exempt from income tax. For the three income years from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028, a Fair Share Contribution of 15% applies to an individual's leviable income (including Mauritian dividends) above MUR 12 million, raising the top rate on large remitted income to 35%. A family that keeps its foreign portfolio income offshore and remits capital pays little or no Mauritian tax.

regimes.name: Mauritian tax resident
regimes.description: Progressive income tax 0/10/20%; foreign income taxed on remittance; temporary 15% Fair Share Contribution above MUR 12 million (2025/26 to 2027/28).
regimes.eligibility: Resident if domiciled in Mauritius (unless permanent abode abroad), present 183 days or more in the income year, or 270 days or more over the income year and the two preceding years. Non-citizens need an occupation or residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: No tax on capital gains. Income from dealings in units and securities is exempt, and foreign capital gains are not taxable. A series of property purchases and resales can be treated as trading.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: No remittance assumption: Mauritius has no capital gains tax (PwC; Deloitte 2026), so gains are 0% whether or not proceeds are brought into Mauritius. Trading in property or securities as a business would be income, and foreign income is taxed when remitted.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Land transfer tax and registration duty on property transactions (rates not verified in this session). Property dealing can be taxed as trade income.
capital_gains.rate_basis: No capital gains tax; securities dealings exempt. Real estate 0% for an investor (land transfer tax, a seller-side transaction tax, is not modelled).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Repeated property buying and selling may be taxed as a trade; income from dealings in securities is expressly exempt.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign capital gains are not taxable whether or not remitted.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by Mauritian resident companies are exempt from income tax, but they count in leviable income for the Fair Share Contribution (15% on leviable income above MUR 12 million, income years 2025/26-2027/28). Foreign dividends are taxable only if received in Mauritius, at up to 20% plus the 15% Fair Share Contribution above MUR 12 million, with a foreign tax credit that usually eliminates much of the Mauritian tax.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Income tax bands from 1 July 2025: first MUR 500,000 at 0%, next MUR 500,000 at 10%, remainder 20%. Fair Share Contribution threshold MUR 12 million of net/leviable income.Fair Share Contribution: 15% on net income above MUR 12 million, for the three income years starting 1 July 2025 (2025/26-2027/28) (PwC; Deloitte Highlights 2026).
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Remittance basis: residents are taxed on Mauritian-source income and on foreign income remitted to Mauritius (MRA; Deloitte 2026). foreign_gross_rate 0.35 is the rate on foreign dividends that ARE remitted (20% top income tax + 15% Fair Share Contribution above MUR 12m). Foreign dividends kept outside Mauritius are taxed at 0%; the scored rate does not assume non-remittance. domestic_rate 0.15 is the Fair Share Contribution on Mauritian dividends above MUR 12m (exempt from income tax).
dividends.important_exceptions: Remittance basis: foreign dividends kept outside Mauritius are not taxed. The Fair Share Contribution applies for income years starting 1 July 2025 and the two following years; it lapses after 30 June 2028 unless extended. Mauritius has over 50 tax treaties (Deloitte 2026) but no comprehensive income tax treaty with the United States (not verified from the MRA treaty list), so US dividends held directly would bear 30% US WHT. Mauritius levies no WHT on dividends paid out (Deloitte 2026).

open_questions: Whether remitted foreign dividends count in full in the income on which the 15% Fair Share Contribution is computed is inferred from 'net income' (PwC, Deloitte), not confirmed from MRA guidance or the Finance Act 2025 text.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: income-tax exempt (Income Tax Act Second Schedule), but 15% Fair Share Contribution on the part of leviable income above MUR 12 million = 0.15 for a large dividend flow. Foreign: 20% top income tax + 15% FSC = 35% on amounts remitted, before foreign tax credit; 0% if not remitted. After June 2028 the FSC is scheduled to lapse (20% / 0%).
dividends.withholding_outbound: Mauritius does not levy WHT on dividends paid by resident companies (general rule; PwC withholding page not checked).
dividends.treaty_network: Network of mostly African and Asian treaties used for holding structures; size not verified. No comprehensive US treaty (not verified).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 15% (80% partial exemption on specified foreign income such as foreign dividends, giving about 3%); GBL companies are used for international holdings. A 5% corporate Fair Share Contribution applies 2025/26-2027/28 to non-GBL companies with chargeable income and supplies above MUR 24 million.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Local rates on property in municipal areas; registration duty on property purchases (rate not verified).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. Whether registration duty applies to transfers of Mauritian property by succession or donation to children was not verified; foreign assets are outside any Mauritian charge.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Registration duty and land transfer tax on Mauritian immovable property may apply on donation (not verified). Mauritian civil law (forced heirship under the Civil Code) restricts free disposition of estates of persons whose succession is governed by Mauritian law (general knowledge; not verified).
inheritance.gift_tax: None; registration duty on gifts of Mauritian real estate not verified.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident for an income year (1 July-30 June) if domiciled in Mauritius unless the permanent place of abode is outside, present 183 days or more in the year, or present 270 days or more in aggregate over the year and the two preceding years.

routes.name: Residence permit through property acquisition / investor occupation permit / Premium Visa
routes.requirements: Mauritius grants residence permits to non-citizens who buy qualifying property (commonly cited minimum USD 375,000) or invest in a business, and Premium Visas for remote workers and retirees; dependants can be included. Amounts and conditions were not verified in this session (the EDB page returned 404).

corporate.summary: 15% CIT (3% for exporters and Freeport operators); 80% partial exemption on specified foreign income (foreign dividends, interest, ship/aircraft leasing) with no foreign tax credit when claimed. Global Business Licence companies taxed at 15%. Corporate Fair Share Contribution 5% (2% for 3% taxpayers) from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028 for companies above MUR 24 million chargeable income and supplies (GBL companies excluded). QDMTT for large MNE groups from 1 July 2025.
corporate.special_zones: Freeport zone (3%), GBL regime for international business.

income.name: Mauritius

income_tax.summary: Resident income tax is 0% to MUR 500,000, 10% on the next MUR 500,000 and 20% above, from 1 July 2025. A Fair Share Contribution of 15% on leviable income above MUR 12 million (income years from 1 July 2025 for three years) lifts the top marginal rate to 35%. Employee CSG is 1.5% on pay up to MUR 50,000 a month and 3% above. Self-employed pay a fixed monthly CSG amount. Foreign-source income of residents is taxed only when remitted.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed CSG is a fixed MUR 150 a month regardless of income (Rogers Capital page, undated, appears to predate 2025 changes): MUR 1,800 a year, about 0.06% of an income of EUR 54,000 (about MUR 2.9 million at roughly MUR 54 per EUR; approximate conversion). Premium Visa holders are reported to be exempt from CSG and NSF under an MRA FAQ (seen via search result only). Employee NSF levy 1% (PwC), CSG employee 1.5% (to MUR 50,000 a month) or 3% above; 3% shown for a high earner.
income_tax.local_tax_note: The 35% band above MUR 12 million is the Fair Share Contribution (15%) added to 20%. Tax year runs 1 July to 30 June; a 2026 income year starts 1 July 2026. A 2026/27 budget reportedly replaces CSG with a National Pensions Fund from July 2027 (not verified).

regimes.name: Mauritius Premium Visa
regimes.description: One-year renewable visa for remote workers, retirees and long-term visitors with foreign income, with no right to local employment. Income Tax Act s.73B (as summarised by Sovereign Group and the Andersen Mauritius Tax Card 2025/26) deems income derived by a Premium Visa holder for work performed remotely from Mauritius to be derived in Mauritius only when it is remitted to Mauritius. So the relief does cover work physically done in Mauritius (covers_local_work true), but only for income left abroad: remitted income is taxed at 0/10/20%; spending through a foreign card is not a remittance, and Mauritian bank deposits are taxable unless tax paid abroad is declared. At 183 days the holder becomes tax resident.
regimes.duration_note: Valid one year, renewable; renewal not guaranteed (Sovereign Group).

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: a tourist visa is usually granted on arrival; stays over 180 days a year need a visa such as the Premium Visa (online application, reported free, processed in about 48 hours). Skilled employees and investors use Occupation Permits (professional, investor, self-employed); an investor permit reportedly needs a transfer of at least USD 50,000. Residence through property starts at USD 375,000 (wiki, secondary).
